OET Sample role-play
ROLEPLAYER CARD                                                                        MEDICINE


SETTING OUTPATIENT CLINIC


PATIENT You returned 5 days ago from a 1 week trip to a country which has a high number of
        COVID-19 cases. You felt fine on the plane and for the first few days, then developed
        cough, runny nose and sore throat. You went on to develop fever, chills and muscle
        aches.You feel like it’s been increasingly hard to breathe and you are breathing more
        quickly than usual. The cough is bringing up some green phlegm.You are worried that it is
        COVID-19.

TASK      • Explain your current symptoms (recent travel from a country with COVID-19 cases,
            mention symptoms, worried about worsening breathing and productive cough.)

          • Be anxious about this shortness of breathing and possibly having this virus because you
            have heard stories of people dying from this virus

          • Refuse to go to the hospital because you are needed at home to take care of your family
            and you insist that you just need an antibiotic.

          • Be frustrated but eventually accept that this is in the best interests of your and your
            family's health and give permission to go to the hospital by ambulance


       CANDIDATE CARD                                                                    MEDICINE
         •

SETTING       OUTPATIENT CLINIC

DOCTOR        The patient has returned from a country which has a high number of COVID-19 cases.
              Over the last 48h he/she has developed fever, chills, body aches as well as nausea,
              vomiting and upper respiratory symptoms. He/she is feeling increasingly short of breath
              and fatigued. The patient hasn’t taken any fever medication today. No diarrhea.


TASK            •   Find out about the patient’s current symptoms and recent travel history

                •   Explain your diagnosis - COVID 19 - and the next steps that you are going to take
                    to confirm. (e.g Chest Xray, blood work, nasal swab for the virus)

                •   Persuade the patient that hospitalisation is needed because of the shortness of
                    breath and need for oxygen, IV fluids and monitoring.

                •   Emphasise the need for hospitalization and personal protective equipment (N95
                    mask, frequent hand washing, isolation for 14 days)

                •   Obtain permission to call the ambulance (safety and speed).
              Role-play Developed by Banfield’s Professional Medical English www.promedicalenglish.com
              Logical Language. Simpler
